  "markdown_report": "**Prioritize padding-safe GRU encoding before another cropping experiment.** At 0% progress, this offers a small, testable intervention grounded in the supplied measurements; localization must precede modification.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) All four categories fail the declared padding tolerance; the latest maximum errors range from 0.00101 to 0.00234. These discrepancies require localization, not automatic attribution to incorrect recurrence. (2) Matched prefix removal reduces margins in every category. These checkpoint interventions do not establish cropped-training benefits. (3) Movies_and_TV has the latest highest sampled misranking rate, 4.92%. Training separation cannot establish host HR@10 or willingness to choose now.

**Related-work insights.** (1) PyTorch’s [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) permit state changes under zero input, motivating explicitly masked recurrence. (2) Its [numerical guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) distinguishes repeatability from batch-shape variation; independent float64 reference checks help isolate semantics. (3) [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) limits generalization to full rankings; [holdout-reuse research](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/5993-generalization-in-adaptive-data-analysis-and-holdout-reuse.pdf) motivates frozen validation queries.

**Framework and directions.** Organize development into encoding correctness, ranking evidence, and context utility:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed next step |
|---|---|---|
| Encoding correctness | Padding discrepancies | Reference equivalence and predictor parity |
| Ranking evidence | Sampled pair margins | Withheld training-prefix rank audits |
| Context utility | Harmful prefix deletion | Matched-supervision cropping after correctness checks |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Canonical padding-safe GRU | 3/7/6 | Reusable correctness foundation | Established method; delicate stochastic equivalence |
| Fixed training-prefix boundary audit | 4/7/4 | Measures top-10 boundary failures | May disagree with host validation |
| Matched-target suffix augmentation | 4/6/5 | Separates context from supervision | Removes useful history; additional cost |

**Selected algorithm.** Preserve the supplied GRU4Rec when already correct. Otherwise gather chronological valid tokens, right-pad internally, pack nonempty rows, run the existing GRU, unpack, and differentiably scatter features. Read the greatest valid original index. Preserve tokenwise transformations; audit temporal normalization and dropout rather than assuming compaction equivalence.

First compare aligned outputs, final states, losses and gradients against copied-weight masked GRUCells in float64 CPU with dropout disabled; then test CUDA, batch composition, causality and predictor reconstruction. Include empty and singleton cases; report numerical errors and top-10 changes without widening thresholds retrospectively.

If correction is necessary, prespecify a padding-only baseline/correction comparison with identical settings, an affordable common final epoch, and two four-category validation sweeps. Charge all attempts against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Preserve seeds, routes, 200 batches/epoch and maximum 200 epochs. Select one complete condition using unchanged macro HR@10; never combine checkpoints. Report paired bootstrap intervals when user outcomes are exposed, conditional on checkpoints and candidates. Validation improvement remains unestablished; one seed and fixed negatives leave additional uncertainty unmeasured.",

    "implementation_notes": "Start from the host's corrected baseline and preserve any implementation already handling padding correctly. Integrate through the supplied interfaces rather than reconstructing unspecified architecture details. Keep embedding transforms, recurrent layers, dropout placement, output transforms, score activation, objective, sampler and optimizer unchanged unless a localized inconsistency requires correction. A zero embedding does not skip GRU updates. Never pack a left-padded tensor directly using nonzero counts: compact real inputs chronologically, pack only nonempty rows, then restore B x L x H alignment. Reset recurrent state for every independent example and layer; preserve gradients through gathered and scattered valid features. Empty rows follow the supplied baseline policy without entering packing or processing a dummy item.

Compaction preserves the intended padding-skipping recurrence, but need not preserve a faulty dense implementation. Tokenwise linear transforms, activations and feature-only LayerNorm preserve valid-token computations under compaction. Time-spanning normalization and training BatchNorm require explicit examination because removing padding can change their statistics. Evaluation BatchNorm requires identical fixed running statistics. Remask padded features after biased transformations. Keep positive and negative IDs aligned with original input positions, preserving causal next-item shifts, valid-position masks and the baseline loss denominator.

Elementwise dropout retains its distribution under compaction, but identical seeds do not guarantee identical token masks after reordering or reshaping. Disable dropout for deterministic equivalence checks, or explicitly share masks in original coordinates and gather them with tokens. Preserve sequence-shared masks where present. Native GRU dropout operates between recurrent layers, excludes the last layer, and is inactive for a single-layer GRU; packed and dense kernels need not consume identical random draws. Do not change production dropout merely to obtain paired stochastic equality. Document any residual stochastic differences in training comparisons.

Build an independent diagnostic reference by copying every existing GRU layer's weight_ih_l{k}, weight_hh_l{k}, bias_ih_l{k} and bias_hh_l{k} into corresponding PyTorch GRUCells. Preserve gate order r,z,n and PyTorch's candidate equation, where reset multiplies the entire recurrent candidate affine result, including its bias. At each timestep process layers bottom-up, masking each layer's state update with the original input-validity mask. Use the same initial states for reference comparisons. Reference copies are unfitted diagnostic implementations of the same parameters, never additional predictors.

Use independent float64 CPU copies, identical inputs and weights, dropout disabled, and a common scalar loss over aligned valid outputs and every layer's final state. Compare valid outputs, final states, scores, losses, input gradients, initial-state gradients and every parameter gradient. Define elementwise agreement as abs(a-b) <= atol + rtol*abs(b), initially using atol=1e-9 and rtol=1e-7 for float64; record maximum errors and failures. Check padded continuous-input gradients against zero with atol=1e-9. Use nonzero diagnostic initial states as an additional gradient check; production state remains freshly zeroed. Skip gradient comparisons for structurally undefined all-empty packing paths and report that exclusion explicitly.

Separately test the actual CUDA float32 inference path. Retain the supplied absolute feature-invariance threshold of 1e-5 and report scale-aware errors using a separately declared relative tolerance of 1e-4. Record nonfinite counts, maximum absolute and relative feature/score errors, counts, score ordering and top-10 changes under fixed eligible candidates and deterministic diagnostic tie handling. Do not silently widen thresholds. Repeated identical execution establishes repeatability only: also test extra leading padding, individual versus batched execution, differing companion lengths, batch permutation and unrelated preceding inference calls. Include empty, singleton, mixed-length, full-length and all-empty batches. Perturb future inputs and verify earlier valid features remain unchanged. Float64 reference agreement supports semantic correctness without proving bitwise CUDA equality.

Use evaluation mode and no gradients for ordinary diagnostic comparisons, then restore the original model mode; run gradient-reference checks separately with gradients enabled. Compare the live model, a freshly reconstructed checkpoint, and the generated predictor using identical item mappings, architecture configuration, histories, candidate IDs and precision. Verify features, scores and top-10 outputs. If the probe uses count-1 on original left-padded coordinates, correct the probe rather than modifying an already-correct model. If padding-safe implementations agree in float64 and discrepancies arise only with CUDA batch shapes, report the numerical issue and its ranking effects before claiming a semantic defect. Retrain from seed 42 whenever production encoding changes.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions with unavailable measurements represented explicitly, never healthy-looking zero defaults. Preserve view.model as the actual nn.Module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Consume batches (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors. Mask sampled-margin positions using nonzero input, positive and negative IDs. The interpretation prompt must use measured metrics and definitions. Margins remain conditional training diagnostics, not ranking accuracy, recommendation diversity or simulator traits.

If localization demonstrates a necessary production correction, predeclare separate baseline and corrected conditions using identical architecture, hyperparameters, initialization seed, sampling streams and training schedule. No training augmentation or loss change belongs in this padding-only comparison. Train fresh models within each authorized condition; do not read or reuse other trials' checkpoints. Use host-provided timing or a charged timing measurement to choose one affordable common final epoch E<=200 before observing condition validation results. Both conditions complete exactly 200 batches per epoch. Use final-epoch checkpoints, avoiding checkpoint searches. If complete conditions cannot fit the remaining budget, report an incomplete comparison rather than changing schedules retrospectively. If the supplied baseline is already correct, retain it and report the diagnostic localization; do not manufacture a correction arm.

For a complete two-condition comparison, cap planned host validation at two four-category sweeps: eight dataset evaluations in total, once per final checkpoint. Record scheduled and actual queries, including partial or failed sweeps, every additional checkpoint evaluation, and inspections of validation results. Do not use validation for implementation debugging. Freeze diagnostic subsets and inspect them during implementation, documenting those inspections separately from validation queries. Select the complete condition with greater equal-weight macro validation HR@10; an exact tie retains the baseline. Select the condition as a whole rather than mixing category winners. Deploy exactly one checkpoint per category, without averaging, fusion, stacking or auxiliary fitted scores.

Define the effect as corrected-minus-baseline macro HR@10, averaging the four category-specific mean paired hit differences. When the host exposes paired per-user hit outcomes on the pinned candidates, perform 10,000 bootstrap replicates with an analysis-only NumPy seed-42 generator: resample 200 users with replacement within each category, preserve baseline/corrected pairs, and average the four resampled category effects. Report category effects, macro effect and two-sided 95% percentile intervals in percentage points. If only aggregates are exposed, report aggregate effects and mark paired intervals unavailable. These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability and do not correct adaptive validation-selection optimism. Do not infer full-catalog performance from sampled HR@10.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs; exactly 200 batches per completed epoch; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; and trial-local artifacts. Update the embedded predictor writer with every production encoding change. Preserve the pinned host evaluator: 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Sum charged runtime across concurrent trials, including training, diagnostics, debugging and failures, against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Four concurrent jobs consume four GPU-seconds per elapsed second while all are running. Record hardware and per-condition expenditure; report LLM time and final held-out inference separately.     "pseudocode": "# Integrate into the supplied model; names below denote its existing pipelines.
# Preserve an already-correct encoder. Do not reconstruct unspecified transforms.

def log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    lengths = valid.sum(dim=1)
    active = lengths.gt(0).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
    output = baseline_zero_position_features(sequence)
    if active.numel() == 0:
        return baseline_empty_position_features(output)

    # Audit normalization/dropout before moving the existing input pipeline.
    # Tokenwise transforms are compatible; temporal transforms need examination.
    compact_ids = right_pad([sequence[b][valid[b]] for b in active])
    embedded = existing_input_pipeline(compact_ids)
    packed = pack_padded_sequence(
        embedded, lengths[active].cpu(),
        batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)
    packed_features, final_states = existing_gru(
        packed, fresh_zero_state_for_all_layers(active))
    compact_features, _ = pad_packed_sequence(
        packed_features, batch_first=True, total_length=compact_ids.shape[1])
    # Unpacking with enforce_sorted=False restores active-row input order.
    compact_features = existing_output_pipeline(compact_features)
    for row, original_row in enumerate(active):
        output[original_row, valid[original_row]] = (
            compact_features[row, :lengths[original_row]])
    return output.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)


def final_features(sequence):
    features = log2feats(sequence)
    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1]).expand_as(sequence)
    final_index = positions.masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
    result = features[arange(sequence.shape[0]), final_index.clamp_min(0)]
    return apply_baseline_empty_history_policy(result, final_index.lt(0))


def masked_reference(continuous_inputs, valid, copied_cells, initial_states):
    states = initial_states
    aligned_outputs = []
    for t in range(continuous_inputs.shape[1]):
        layer_input = continuous_inputs[:, t]
        for layer, cell in enumerate(copied_cells):
            proposed = cell(layer_input, states[layer])
            states[layer] = where(valid[:, t, None], proposed, states[layer])
            layer_input = states[layer]  # current lower-layer state
        aligned_outputs.append(where(valid[:, t, None], layer_input, 0))
    return stack(aligned_outputs, dim=1), states

# Localization, using no additional fitted model:
# 1. Fix diagnostic histories/candidates and define tolerances before inspection.
# 2. Copy identical GRU weights into float64 CPU packed and masked references.
# 3. Disable dropout; compare aligned valid outputs, every final state and scores.
# 4. Use the same scalar loss and compare inputs, initial states and all gradients.
# 5. Check empty/singleton/mixed/full/all-empty cases and causal prefix invariance.
# 6. Separately characterize CUDA float32 padding and batch-shape sensitivity.
# 7. Compare live model, fresh checkpoint reconstruction and generated predictor.
# 8. Preserve/restore mode and retain all required diagnosis and ModelView APIs.

# Only if production encoding requires correction:
# Predeclare baseline/corrected conditions, common final E<=200, query cap=8
# dataset evaluations, macro criterion, baseline-on-tie rule and affordable budget.
# In separate authorized experiments, train a fresh model/category/condition
# with preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42 and 200 batches/completed epoch.
# Keep original targets, negatives, causal shifts, masks and loss normalization.
# Save final checkpoints and matching predictor code beneath each trial directory.
# Obtain one unchanged host validation sweep per complete condition.
# If paired user hits exist, bootstrap users within categories: 10,000 draws,
# analysis seed 42, equal category weights, 95% percentile intervals.
# Select one entire condition; deploy exactly one checkpoint per category.
# Never combine scores or checkpoints, and never inspect other trials.",
